turns.text: What stands out in my mind is you know, I really had this whole thing in my head how it was gonna go, right? And it completely did not go that way. [laughs]

turns.text: Well you know, and I think that's a good thing. It turned into such a conversation around the, the, you know the direction that we were going as a company, around the product, and around where the market was going. It kind of. It actually went a lot better than I had anticipated.

turns.speaker: Josh
turns.text: Really?

turns.text: Um. And I think part of the reason was. You know I really do believe that the investors liked what they saw in our model and in what we had done. turns.speaker: Josh

turns.text: I’ve never even asked that question before.

turns.text: You’re kidding.

turns.text: No, I’m not. I can tell you what my mindset was. And kind of, what I was thinking. First of all, I qualified the heck out of it, right? Like, I’ve never done this before, thought about it that much, but this is something that’s come into my mind now.

turns.speaker: Josh
turns.text: That really hit you in the moment?

turns.speaker: Kevin
turns.text: It did, it did. And what I was thinking was you know, the conversation is going so well, but I feel the resistance, right, from the investors, I feel it based on traction. turns.text: That’s exactly right. So what I thought in my head is like, can I do, you know, can I essentially get a small campaign funded as a proof of concept. turns.text: You just wanted them to think creatively. Like, okay what would it take for you guys to make a deal here today.

turns.speaker: Kevin
turns.text: That’s right. Total hail mary, but you know, my son’s favorite team is the Green Bay Packers. Aaron Rodgers does it all the time. You know, sometimes you make a catch, right?

turns.text:
